title: The MTBF ladder
caption: Expected hours between GPU failures collapse as the fleet grows: one device at 50,000 h, 1,000 at 50 h, 10,000 at 5 h, with the full-system cascade and the Llama 3 measurement marked below the GPU-only line.
alt: Bar chart of expected hours between GPU failures on a log scale across fleet sizes 1, 1,000, and 10,000 GPUs, with a dashed mark for the ~3.9 h full-system value and ~3.1 h measured Llama 3 cadence.

title: The Young-Daly floor
caption: Save overhead falls hyperbolically while expected rework climbs linearly with the interval; their sum has a shallow minimum near 14 minutes, where the two terms are equal. Being off the optimum is cheap; being far off is not.
alt: Plot of wall-time waste vs checkpoint interval: a falling dashed write-overhead curve, a rising dashed rework line, and a solid total curve with a shallow marked minimum at ~14 min / ~5.9%, tinted writes-dominate left and rework-dominate right.

title: The 6.6-minute recovery budget
caption: One cold restart decomposed: detect ~30 s, restart ~4 min, load ~24.5 s, warmup ~2 min. Restart and warmup dominate the budget — the checkpoint read everyone worries about is the small term.
alt: Horizontal stacked timeline of the four recovery terms totaling ~6.6 minutes, with restart and warmup drawn as the long segments and detect/load as thin ones.

title: Detection layers
caption: Escalating detection depth: liveness probes catch dead processes, heartbeat timeouts catch hangs, inference checks catch wrong answers, and progress-median comparison catches the straggler that passes every liveness check while halving the job.
alt: Four stacked detection layers from liveness to progress-median, each labeled with the failure class it catches and the one that slips through.
